headline: B4 (delay/interference capacity curves) and B5 (variable-N and cell-permutation equivariance) materialized: 812 + 1828 = 2640 rendered candidate rows, both fail-closed leakage-audited clean after one caught-and-fixed real leak.
state: Gabriel's direct instruction (relayed 2026-08-26): 10,000 total training examples needed for the full fine-tune, work parallelized 4-way (B0 done, B1 done, B6 done by sibling agents; this agent covers B4+B5 concurrently with the sibling covering B2+B3). Per the course's 'rebase/audit the strongest existing donor rather than creating a competing generator' guidance: evaluated reusing tools/trigger2_dynamic_binding_blueprint_v2.py (the B0/B1 donor) first, but it is architecturally pinned to N=3 via full-S3-permutation machinery and has no capacity/delay or variable-N axis at all -- extending it would graft an unrelated axis onto a donor built for a different question, risking the exact confound the course warns against. Wrote two new generators instead, sharing only the donor's provenance metadata constants (MODEL/MODEL_REV/SOURCE_PACKAGE_SHA256/ABI_MANIFEST_SHA256) for corpus-wide ancestry consistency: tools/trigger2_b4_capacity_interference_generator_v1.py and tools/trigger2_b5_variable_n_equivariance_generator_v1.py, each self-contained generator+audit+writer (no separate donor to materialize), fail-closed (refuses to write output JSONL if its own audit does not pass). Atom pools and (for B5) entity namespaces are kept disjoint per family (B0/B1: ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:00-14; B4: 20-99 real+decoy; B5: 200-299) so no cross-family atom collision is even possible, plus standard within-family TRAIN/VALIDATION-shared vs HOLDOUT_FROZEN-disjoint pools. REAL BUG CAUGHT AND FIXED (governance model working as designed, same as the B0/B1 blueprint-v2 leakage correction earlier this session): B5's first version resampled a fresh entity subset per episode and ran the bag-of-words shortcut probe as naive row-level 5-fold CV; this let entity-name-alone predict target at 86% (chance ~20%) because too few episodes reused each entity with independently fresh atom draws AND because rows from the same episode (identical eq_text/target, differing only in presentation order, which eq_text excludes by design) leaked across CV folds. Fixed by (1) making entity SETS canonical per N-level and reused across all episode repeats -- forcing each entity name to be queried across many episodes with fresh atom draws -- and (2) deduplicating by (episode_id, queried_entity) before cross-validating, since duplicate presentation-order rows are not independent observations for a lexical-shortcut probe. Reproduced the fix empirically before accepting: 86% -> 54% (still failing, entity-set fix alone insufficient) -> 20.6% vs 22.8% chance (passing) after the CV-dedup fix. Also caught and fixed a reproducibility bug during development: B5's sampled-permutation path built presentation orders via a Python set, whose iteration order depends on PYTHONHASHSEED (randomized per process by default) -- two runs with identical seeded RNGs produced the same rows in different order (different output bytes). Fixed by sorting before return; verified byte-identical output across PYTHONHASHSEED-varied reruns for both B4 and B5 (added as a regression test in both test files, not just asserted). B4: 812 rows (420 TRAIN/210 VALIDATION/182 HOLDOUT_FROZEN) sweeping capacity K in {2,4,8,16} (top end matches the declared <=16 whitened-HRR safe-binding guarantee from course section 4) crossed with delay D in {0,2,4,8} and interference_kind in {NONE,NEUTRAL,LOOKALIKE} (lookalike = decoy codebook-shaped lines for entities/atoms NOT in the episode, real interference vs pure delay). B5: 1828 rows (940/564/324) covering N in {2,3,4,6,8,12}, exact full S_N permutation crossing at N in {2,3} and 6 distinct sampled permutations at N in {4,6,8,12} (12!=479001600, exhaustive is infeasible), with the core checked property being exact per-(episode,entity) target invariance across every tested presentation order -- the literal cell-permutation-equivariance claim in the family name, not a proxy for it. 17/17 pytest tests pass across both new test files (10 for B4, includes cross-process determinism check; the equivariance invariant, presentation-order-count, holdout-disjointness and the CV-dedup regression are separately asserted for B5). accepted_dataset_tokens remains 0; training_credit remains 0 -- candidate/quarantined materialization per TRIGGERWORT_2 course Step 6, not an admission event. Honesty note carried into both generator docstrings: family-disjointness, target-derivation and decoy/filler-leak checks are exact (recomputed over every row); the bag-of-words probe remains an empirical secondary corroboration, not an exact-enumeration proof (B4's docstring explicitly disclaims a presentation-order MI-exactness claim it does not make, unlike blueprint_v2's leakage audit).
next: 2640 rows (B4+B5) plus the sibling families (B0 72+540, B1 9072, B6 unknown row count) likely exceeds Gabriel's rough ~2500-per-family / 10k-total guidance in aggregate, same open question the B1 receipt flagged for chatgpt-secondary and still apparently unresolved -- worth a combined curation/selection pass across all six families before any admission attempt, rather than each family independently maximizing its own row count. Real ABI atom manifest + pinned tokenizer binding remain the blocking gate before any of B0/B1/B4/B5/B6 can move past candidate/quarantined status, per the same course document and Q35 identity-metrology chain referenced in every prior receipt this session.
